sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32, and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. They say that something happened or went on in spite of a difficulty. With a real fact the verb is in the indicative. That is the story of the Nicaraguan 1980s: a campaign that went on in spite of attacks, a community that painted in spite of poverty.

sections.title: Forms with a pesar de and pese a
rows: A pesar de los ataques, la campaña siguió.
*a pesar de* + noun: in spite of the attacks, the campaign went on
A pesar de ser muy pobres, empezaron a pintar.
*a pesar de* + infinitive: although they were very poor, they began to paint
A pesar de que había guerra, hubo elecciones en 1990.
*a pesar de que* + a full clause: although there was war, there were elections in 1990
Pese a la guerra, la escuela siguió abierta.
*pese a* + noun: despite the war, the school stayed open

items.spanish: A pesar de los ataques, miles de jóvenes enseñaron a leer a campesinos.
items.english: In spite of the attacks, thousands of young people taught peasants to read.

items.spanish: Los campesinos de Solentiname empezaron a pintar a pesar de no tener estudios de arte.
items.english: The peasants of Solentiname began to paint although they had no art training.

items.spanish: A pesar de que la comunidad fue destruida en 1977, las pinturas de Solentiname son famosas.
items.english: Although the community was destroyed in 1977, the paintings of Solentiname are famous.

items.spanish: Pese a los años de guerra, en 1990 hubo elecciones en Nicaragua.
items.english: Despite the years of war, there were elections in Nicaragua in 1990.

sections.content: Before a full clause you need *que*: *a pesar de que había guerra*. Before a noun or an infinitive you do not: *a pesar de la guerra*, *a pesar de ser pobres*. Not *a pesar que*, and not *a pesar de había guerra*.
